nodes.summary: For coprime natural numbers $m, n > 1$, the Carmichael function $\lambda$ satisfies $\lambda(mn) = \operatorname{lcm}(\lambda(m), \lambda(n))$.
nodes.title: Carmichael's function on coprime products

nodes.summary: Let $\lambda$ be the Carmichael function and, for natural numbers $p$ and $m$, let $v_p(m)$ be the exponent of $p$ in the prime factorization of $m$ (taken to be $0$ when $p$ is not prime or $m = 0$). For natural numbers $q$ and $n$, the natural number $\Delta_q(n)$ is defined as follows. nodes.title: The count $\Delta_q(n)$ for primitive λ-roots

nodes.summary: Let $\lambda$ be the Carmichael function, and let $\Delta_q$ and $h_q$ be the count and the local factor for primitive λ-roots. Let $m, n > 1$ be coprime natural numbers and let $q$ be a prime dividing $\lambda(mn)$. Then $h_q(m)\,h_q(n) \le h_q(mn)$. Moreover, $h_q(m)\,h_q(n) < h_q(mn)$ if and only if at least one of the following holds: $0 < \Delta_q(m) < \Delta_q(mn)$; $0 < \Delta_q(n) < \Delta_q(mn)$; or…
nodes.title: Huang–Li inequality for the local factors $h_q$

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta_q(n)$ be the count for primitive λ-roots. For natural numbers $q$ and $n$, the rational number $h_q(n)$ equals $1$ if $\Delta_q(n) = 0$, and $1 - 1/q^{\Delta_q(n)}$ otherwise.
nodes.title: The local factor $h_q(n)$ for primitive λ-roots

nodes.summary: Let $R(n)$ be the number of primitive λ-roots modulo $n$. For coprime natural numbers $m, n > 1$, we have $R(m)\,R(n) \le R(mn)$, and $R(mn) = R(m)\,R(n)$ if and only if $m = 2$ and $n$ is odd, or $n = 2$ and $m$ is odd.
nodes.title: Supermultiplicativity of the number of primitive λ-roots

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $R(n)$ is the number of units $a$ of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ whose multiplicative order equals $\lambda(n)$, where $\lambda$ is the Carmichael function.
nodes.title: Number of primitive λ-roots

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
